title: MAS-ISP: A Proxy-Free Online Hyperparameter Optimization Framework for ISP Hardware System
problem: Real-time Image Signal Processors (ISPs) for autonomous driving must adapt dynamically to varying lighting/weather conditions, but traditional offline or proxy-based tuning cannot respond quickly to environmental changes; manual hyperparameter tuning is infeasible at runtime.
motivation: Autonomous systems require real-time visual quality adaptation; stale or proxy-based ISP tuning degrades perception accuracy in dynamic environments.
method: The system uses multiple AI agents trained with reinforcement learning—learning which settings produce good results by trying configurations and receiving reward signals—to adjust Image Signal Processor (ISP) parameters in real-time, without needing a proxy model as an intermediary. A master agent coordinates the others to ensure consistent adjustments across consecutive video frames. Two hardware optimizations, Strip Convolution Kernel and Stride-Aware Dual-Buffer Memory, reduce the neural network computation required for image processing, enabling real-time operation on FPGA or ASIC hardware.
key_novelty: Instead of using offline tuning or a proxy model, this system uses multiple AI agents trained with reinforcement learning to adjust Image Signal Processor (ISP) settings in real-time as the car drives, responding instantly to lighting and weather changes.
contributions: Proxy-free online DRL-based hyperparameter optimization for ISP
Multi-agent master-slave system for cooperative parameter tuning
Hardware innovations: Strip Convolution Kernel, Stride-Aware Dual-Buffer Memory
1080P@75FPS/240FPS on FPGA/ASIC platforms; inter-frame consistency improvement
limitations: Evaluation on autonomous driving only; generalization to other vision tasks; DRL convergence time in highly dynamic scenes; energy profiling for FPGA/ASIC not detailed.
primary_theme: real-time proxy-free ISP tuning via distributed DRL for autonomous vision systems
